packages.name: io.mutastic.annotations
packages.doc:
Annotations for code mutastic tests: [`DoNotMutate`](donotmutate/) to skip, [`DoMutate`](domutate/) to keep what would be
skipped. Read from the class files, so they cost nothing at run time.

types.name: DoMutate
types.summary: mutastic mutates this method, or every method of this class, even where it would skip it as arid: a `toString()` that customers see, a getter that is a contract.
types.doc:
mutastic mutates this method, or every method of this class, even where it would skip it as
arid: a `toString()` that customers see, a getter that is a contract.

members.name: value
members.doc: Why it matters: for the reader.

types.name: DoNotMutate
types.summary: mutastic skips the mutants in this method, or in every method of this class, and reports them as skipped with `value` as the reason: `@DoNotMutate("measured by the load tests")`.
types.doc:
mutastic skips the mutants in this method, or in every method of this class, and reports them as
skipped with `value` as the reason: `@DoNotMutate("measured by the load tests")`.

members.name: value
members.doc: Why: shown with each skipped mutant.

types.name: BuildTool
types.summary: A build tool mutastic reads a project's setup from, found with `java.util.ServiceLoader`: each is asked in turn whether a directory is one of its builds.
types.doc:
A build tool mutastic reads a project's setup from, found with `java.util.ServiceLoader`: each
is asked in turn whether a directory is one of its builds.

members.name: name
members.doc: `Gradle`: how messages name it.

members.name: buildFiles
members.doc:
The files that make a directory one of its builds, as a person would look for them:
`settings.gradle(.kts) or build.gradle(.kts)`.

members.name: recognises
members.doc: Whether `directory` is one of its builds.

members.name: workDirectory
members.doc:
Where a module keeps mutastic's run record, logs and reports, so each module keeps its own:
`build/mutastic` for the build in `directory`, `build/mutastic/data` for `:data`.

members.name: dependents
members.signature: default List<String> dependents(Path directory, String module, Path workDirectory)
members.doc:
The modules whose tests can reach `module`'s code: the ones that depend on it, directly or
through others, in the tool's own names for them (`:app`).

members.name: read
members.signature: Project read(Path directory, String module, Path workDirectory, String typed)
members.doc: The module's code and tests, and how its build runs them.

params.name: module

params.name: typed

throws.name: SetupFailed
throws.doc: when the build can't be read, saying what to do instead

members.name: DEFAULT_SUITE
members.doc: The test suite a run uses unless told otherwise: Gradle's `test` task, Maven's Surefire.

members.name: read
members.doc:
The module's code and the tests of one of its suites, and how its build runs them. A tool with
one suite has only [`DEFAULT_SUITE`](#default_suite).

throws.name: SetupFailed
throws.doc: when the build has no such suite, saying which it has

members.name: read
members.signature: Project read(Path directory, String module, Path setup)
members.doc:
The module's code and tests from `setup`, a file in [`ProjectSetup`](../projectsetup/)'s format the build already
wrote: for an entry point inside the build, such as a build plugin, which needn't run it
again. Named as [`read(Path, String, Path, String)`](#read) names it, so their runs compare.

members.name: noSuite
members.doc:
What a build says when it has no suite of that name, from its log: the line after `mutastic:
no test suite `, if it said so.

members.name: ID_HINT
members.doc: For someone who ran a command that names a mutant from somewhere else.

types.name: BuiltIn
types.summary: mutastic's own operators.
types.doc:
mutastic's own operators. How each finds its sites and rewrites them is the engine's. Internal,
as operators join and leave mutastic's own set in minor releases, with their scoring changes: a
plugin names an operator by its [`id`](#id), as rules and `--operators` do.

members.name: COMPARISON
members.doc:
In `stronger`: with [`BOUNDARY`](#boundary)'s edge moved and [`REMOVE_CONDITIONAL`](#remove_conditional)'s condition always true
or false, the smallest set of changes whose catches catch every other change of a comparison.
For `a < b` that's `a <= b` (boundary), `a != b` (this one) and `false`. Measured on
mutastic's own code (6 Nov 2026), most of its misses were noise: counters that count up to
their end, sizes compared with a value they never pass.

members.name: OTHER_COMPARISON
members.doc:
In `stronger`: the rest of what a comparison can become, and a condition the other way round,
as `mutastic/negate-conditional` was, which it replaced (6 Nov 2026). A test that catches the
mutants of [`BOUNDARY`](#boundary), [`COMPARISON`](#comparison) and [`REMOVE_CONDITIONAL`](#remove_conditional) catches these too, so in the
defaults their catches would only add to the score.

members.name: RETURN_VALUE
members.doc:
Replaced `mutastic/return-default` (6 Nov 2026), which returned each type's default: a `return
false` already returned it, and `null` is rarely what a method returning a list gets wrong.

members.name: REMOVE_DISCARDED_CALL
members.doc:
A call whose result is thrown away, removed: `list.add(item);`, `map.put(key, value);`,
`text.append(more);`. Its result isn't used, so only what it does matters, as with a call that
returns nothing. A fluent call that returns its receiver is no different: removing
`builder.append(x);` loses the append.

members.name: REMOVE_ASSIGNMENT
members.doc:
An assignment to a local variable that already has a value, removed: it keeps that value. A
declaration's first value isn't changed, as the code wouldn't load without it.

members.name: REMOVE_FIELD_WRITE
members.doc:
A write to a field, removed: it keeps the value it had. Constructors and static initialisers
are left alone, as for every operator, and a plain setter is arid, so what's left is state a
method changes.

members.name: OMIT_CALL
members.doc:
A call that only wraps a value, left out, so the value goes on as it was: the missing
`escape(text)`. Only for the calls the engine can be sure of, as a call that returns the type
it's given can still change what it holds.

members.name: SWAP_ARGUMENTS
members.doc: A call's last two arguments, where they have the same type, swapped: the compiler can't tell.

members.name: NULL_PARAMETER
members.doc:
A parameter that holds an object, set to `null` as the method starts: a value the method may
not really need, or a caller's `null` it doesn't handle.

members.name: DROP_VARARG
members.doc: An array built for a call on the spot, usually a varargs call's, without its last element.

members.name: LOGICAL_CONNECTOR
members.doc:
`&&` to `||` and back. javac has no opcode for either, so the engine finds the two jumps javac
writes for a condition of two tests joined by one, and turns the first round.

members.name: OTHER_ARITHMETIC
members.doc:
In `stronger`: every other change of `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and `%`, on all four number types,
beyond what [`MATH`](#math) and [`ARITHMETIC_REPLACEMENT`](#arithmetic_replacement) make, whose ids stay as they are.

members.name: BITWISE
members.doc:
In `stronger`, as the Rust edition has it: `&`, `|` and `^` each to the other two, and the
shifts. `~x` (javac's `x ^ -1`) isn't changed, and `&=` and `|=` never become `^=`.

members.name: KEEP_OPERAND
members.doc:
A calculation down to one of its operands. Both are still worked out, so a call in the other
still runs. A constant beside a variable isn't what's kept: nothing plausibly forgets it.

members.name: CONSTANT_VALUE
members.doc:
A number in the code changed, including a `static final` one: javac writes its value where
it's used, so a threshold set wrong shows here and nowhere else. Numbers that can't be told
from a `boolean`, and those javac writes itself, are left alone.

members.name: FLIP_INCREMENT
members.doc:
A variable's own step the other way: `iinc` with its sign flipped. Most are loop counters, and
a loop that never ends costs a whole time limit to catch, so it's in `stronger`.

members.name: REMOVE_NEGATION
members.doc: A negation taken away: `-x` becomes `x`.

members.name: REMOVE_SWITCH_ARM
members.doc:
One entry of a switch sent to its default. javac's own parts have none: a `String` switch's
hash lookup, and the default it writes for a switch with no need of one. Where that default
throws, the arm's values throw, which is what the mutant really does, so the card says so.

members.name: REPLACE_BODY
members.doc:
A whole method's code replaced, as a fast first pass: it finds a method no test notices at
all. Finer operators' mutants subsume it, so a catch here says little; a miss says a lot.

members.name: DROP_CATCH_TYPE
members.doc: Experimental: no study shows what these catch. One type of a `catch (A | B e)` taken out.

members.name: REMOVE_THROW
members.doc:
Experimental: no study shows what these catch. A `throw` gone, and the code carries on, where
that verifies: at the end of a method nothing comes next, and the mutant is unviable.

members.name: STRING_CONSTANT
members.doc:
A string in the code emptied. What only tells a person something is arid: what goes into a log
call, an exception or a failed check.

members.name: REGEX_CONSTANT
members.doc:
A regular expression that goes straight into a call, changed to one that still compiles. It
runs in static initialisers and constructors too, as a `Pattern` is usually a field.

members.name: first
members.doc:
One of the operators whose mutants' ids were fixed before operators were open: their ids leave
the operator out, and stay as they were. Every other operator's put it in, including
[`OTHER_COMPARISON`](#other_comparison), which replaced the negated condition: its ids changed with it.

types.name: ChangedLines
types.signature: @Internal record ChangedLines(String since, Map<Path, Set<Integer>> lines)
types.summary: The source lines a change touched, by file: what a run scoped to a change mutates.
types.doc:
The source lines a change touched, by file: what a run scoped to a change mutates. Lines only a
deletion touched aren't here, since there's no code left on them to mutate.

params.name: since
params.doc: what the change is measured from, as given: `main`, `HEAD`

params.name: lines
params.doc: each changed source file, absolute, and its changed lines, from 1

members.name: covers
members.doc: Whether `line` of `file` (absolute) changed.

members.name: within
members.doc: Only the files under `roots`: one module's sources, of a change across a repository.

types.name: ClassMutator
types.summary: An operator a plugin adds that changes a class as a whole, where a [`Mutator`](../mutator/) changes one instruction: what no instruction holds, as an annotation on a class or a field, or a method written anew.
types.doc:
An operator a plugin adds that changes a class as a whole, where a [`Mutator`](../mutator/) changes one
instruction: what no instruction holds, as an annotation on a class or a field, or a method
written anew. Plugins provide theirs as a `java.util.ServiceLoader` service, in a jar
`mutastic.yaml` lists under `plugins:`.

A mutant of one runs with every class loaded anew, as what reads an annotation may have kept
what it read, and a class written anew may have methods the build's doesn't: swapping it into
the class already loaded wouldn't reach either. That costs a load of the classes, and whatever a
test sets up on them, for each mutant.

Each mutant's id is made from its member, its change's label and the operator's id, so a label
must never change once released.

members.name: changes
members.doc:
The changes this operator makes in `owner`, each by its member and label; none when it doesn't
apply.

members.name: write
members.signature: byte[] write(ClassModel owner, ClassMutator.Member member, String label)
members.doc:
`owner`'s bytes with the change made. A change that doesn't verify, or that throws an
`IllegalArgumentException` or `IllegalStateException` here, is skipped as unviable, never run.

members.name: words
members.doc: What a missed mutant's card says.

members.name: prepare
members.doc:
Told of the project before any of its classes, for an operator that needs more than the class
file: to compile against its classpath, or read its sources.

members.name: reach
members.doc: Which tests a mutant runs against.

types.name: ClassMutator.Change
types.signature:
record Change(
    ClassMutator.Member member,
    String label,
    String original,
    String sourceText,
    Optional<String> skipped)
types.summary: One change to a class.
types.doc: One change to a class.

params.name: member
params.doc: what it's on

params.name: label
params.doc: what it becomes, short: `remove @NotNull`

params.name: original
params.doc: what's there now: `@NotNull`

params.name: sourceText
params.doc: the text that marks its line in the source, `@NotNull`, for the line a card shows: class files have no line for an annotation. Empty when nothing does

params.name: skipped
params.doc: why it shouldn't run, if it shouldn't, kind first: `equivalent: …`

members.name: of
members.signature: static ClassMutator.Change of(ClassMutator.Member member, String label, String original, String sourceText)

types.name: ClassMutator.Member
types.summary: What a change is on: a method, a field or the class itself.
types.doc:
What a change is on: a method, a field or the class itself. Its name and descriptor stand in
for a mutant's method, in its id and in what reports show.

params.name: name
params.doc: the method's name, `<field total>`, or `<class>`

params.name: descriptor
params.doc: the method's or the field's descriptor; empty for the class

members.name: ofClass
members.doc: The class itself.

members.name: ofField
members.signature: static ClassMutator.Member ofField(String name, String descriptor)

members.name: simpleName
members.doc: The field's name, for a field; the method's, for a method; empty for the class.

types.name: ClassMutator.Reach
types.summary: Which tests can notice a change.
types.doc:
Which tests can notice a change. Coverage says which tests reach a line, and a change with no
line needs another way to say it.

members.name: EVERY_TEST
members.doc:
Every test: those that reach the class first, each set fastest first, stopping at the first
failure. For what's read by reflection: a test that a method's `@PreAuthorize` denies never
runs a line of it, and the class was made while a framework started up, in no test. A mutant
no test notices costs a run of every test.

members.name: METHOD
members.doc:
The tests that reach a line of the mutant's method, fastest first; none, and it's not
covered. For a method that changes what it does when it runs.

types.name: Comparison
types.signature:
@Internal record Comparison(
    OptionalDouble previousScore,
    boolean sameCode,
    boolean sameTool,
    List<Comparison.Flip> flips)
types.summary: This run against the last one.
types.doc:
This run against the last one.

With the code and mutastic unchanged, a mutant is caught or missed the same way every time
unless a test behaves differently between runs. So a mutant that was caught last run and is
missed now, or the other way round, points at the test that caught it: likely flaky. With either
changed, a flip is just the change at work.

params.name: previousScore
params.doc: the last run's score; none when it had no mutants to score

params.name: sameCode
params.doc: whether the code and tests are byte for byte what the last run had

params.name: sameTool
params.doc: whether the same mutastic ran

params.name: flips
params.doc: mutants caught in one run and not the other

members.name: sameness
members.doc: `same code`, `code changed` or `mutastic changed`: what explains a difference.

members.name: likelyFlaky
members.doc:
Each likely flaky test and the mutants whose results it changed: empty unless the code and
mutastic are the same.

types.name: Comparison.Flip
types.signature:
record Flip(
    String id,
    Status before,
    Status after,
    Optional<String> caughtBy)
types.summary: A mutant caught in one run and not the other.
types.doc: A mutant caught in one run and not the other.

params.name: caughtBy
params.doc: the test that caught it, in whichever run it was caught; empty for a timeout

types.name: CoveragePass
types.signature:
@Internal record CoveragePass(
    int jdk,
    int tests,
    Duration took,
    int mutants,
    List<String> flaky,
    List<FlakyTest> flakyEvidence)
types.summary: What the coverage pass found, before any mutant runs.
types.doc: What the coverage pass found, before any mutant runs.

params.name: jdk
params.doc: the feature version the tests run on

params.name: tests
params.doc: how many tests ran

params.name: took
params.doc: how long the pass took

params.name: mutants
params.doc: how many will run (or be reported as skipped or not covered)

params.name: flaky
params.doc: tests left out because they failed and then passed

params.name: flakyEvidence
params.doc: for each flaky test, what it failed with and what it reaches that changes from run to run

members.name: CoveragePass
members.signature: CoveragePass(int jdk, int tests, Duration took, int mutants, List<String> flaky)
members.doc: A pass with nothing known of why its flaky tests are flaky.

types.name: Filter
types.summary: Decides that a method's mutants shouldn't run, and says why.
types.doc:
Decides that a method's mutants shouldn't run, and says why. A filter acts only on positive
evidence in the bytecode, never on a name alone: one that skips too much makes the score lie,
and nobody can tell.

members.name: id
members.doc: `mutastic:trivial-accessors`: how configuration and audits name it.

members.name: prepare
members.doc:
Sees the whole module's classes once, before any [`skip`](#skip): a filter that judges a method by who
calls it needs them all.

members.name: skip
members.doc: Why `method`'s mutants shouldn't run, if they shouldn't.

types.name: FlakyTest
types.signature:
@Internal record FlakyTest(
    String test,
    List<String> failure,
    List<String> reaches,
    List<String> reachesInTest,
    boolean failsAlone)
types.summary: What a flaky test's failure and reach say about why it's flaky: the difference between a test that's its own doing (an unseeded `Random`, the clock), which can be made to give the same answer every time, and one that reaches outside the code (the network, a database), where changing the test or the code to get past it would hide what's wrong.
types.doc:
What a flaky test's failure and reach say about why it's flaky: the difference between a test
that's its own doing (an unseeded `Random`, the clock), which can be made to give the same
answer every time, and one that reaches outside the code (the network, a database), where
changing the test or the code to get past it would hide what's wrong.

params.name: test
params.doc: the test, as `com.example.QuoteClientTest#aPriceComesFromTheFeed`

params.name: failure
params.doc: the exception it failed with and its causes, outermost first, by class name; empty when the worker didn't say

params.name: reaches
params.doc: calls the code the test ran makes that give a different answer from one run to the next: `new Random()`, `Instant.now`, `System.nanoTime`

params.name: reachesInTest
params.doc: the same, in the test's own class: its set-up, a stand-in it starts. A test whose own code varies makes its own flakiness, even when it fails on the network: a stand-in feed with a random delay times out by the test's doing, not the network's.

params.name: failsAlone
params.doc: it passed among the others, caught mutants, and failed on its own with no mutant in when run again after them: it counts on something another test or the run sets up or leaves behind, so its catches say nothing about a mutant, and the run doesn't pass

members.name: FlakyTest
members.signature: FlakyTest(String test, List<String> failure, List<String> reaches, List<String> reachesInTest)

members.name: failingAlone
members.doc: The same test, known to fail on its own.

members.name: failedOutside
members.doc:
Whether it failed with something from outside the code: an exception, or a cause of one, from
the network, a database, a channel or a file, or a timeout waiting on one.

members.name: failedWith
members.doc: The exception it failed with, by its simple name, if the worker said.

members.name: outsideCause
members.doc: The innermost cause from outside the code, by simple name: `HttpTimeoutException`.

types.name: Ghost
types.signature:
@Internal record Ghost(
    MutantResult result,
    String field,
    String property,
    Ghost.Rule rule,
    List<Ghost.Peer> peers,
    int writes)
types.summary: A ghost: an insertion mutant, for code that most sites like this one have and this one lacks.
types.doc:
A ghost: an insertion mutant, for code that most sites like this one have and this one lacks. It
adds the call the majority makes, here a property change that a write doesn't announce where its
peers do, and the tests that reach the write run against it. It's experimental, and never in the
score: a ghost no test notices is a question about what the code should do, not a gap the score
should count.

A ghost *appears* when a test notices the inserted call, which says that test expects the
silence, and *passes unseen* when none does.

params.name: result
params.doc: the inserted call's run: caught is appeared, missed is passed unseen

params.name: field
params.doc: the field the write is to

params.name: property
params.doc: the property name the inserted call fires

params.name: rule
params.doc: why mutastic thinks the call belongs there

params.name: peers
params.doc: the writes that do announce themselves, that the call was copied from

params.name: writes
params.doc: how many writes the rule counted, this one among them: of the field, for [`Rule#SAME_FIELD`](../rule/#same_field); of the class's properties, one per field, for [`Rule#SIBLING_FIELDS`](../rule/#sibling_fields)

members.name: appeared
members.doc: Whether a test noticed the inserted call.

members.name: passedUnseen
members.doc: Whether every test that reaches the write passed with the call in.

types.name: Ghost.Peer
types.signature: record Peer(String method, int line, String property)
types.summary: A write that does fire: where it is, and the property it names.
types.doc: A write that does fire: where it is, and the property it names.

params.name: method
params.doc: the method's name, `deposit`

types.name: Ghost.Rule
types.summary: Why a missing call looks missing.
types.doc: Why a missing call looks missing.

members.name: SAME_FIELD
members.doc: Other writes to the same field fire a property change, and this one doesn't.

members.name: SIBLING_FIELDS
members.doc:
The class's other properties fire a property change on every write, and this setter's
doesn't.

types.name: Ignore
types.signature:
@Internal record Ignore(
    String id,
    String code,
    String reason,
    String kind)
types.summary: A mutant the project has decided not to test, by id, from `.mutastic/ignores.yaml`: written by `mutastic ignore`, committed, and reviewed like code.
types.doc:
A mutant the project has decided not to test, by id, from `.mutastic/ignores.yaml`: written by
`mutastic ignore`, committed, and reviewed like code.

params.name: code
params.doc: the source line the mutant was on, trimmed, when it was ignored: once the line changes, the decision no longer holds and the mutant runs again

params.name: kind
params.doc: what sort of decision it is, one of [`KINDS`](#kinds), or empty when it doesn't say

members.name: Ignore
members.signature: Ignore(String id, String code, String reason)
members.doc: A decision that doesn't say its sort.

members.name: KINDS
members.doc:
The sorts of decision: the change can't be told apart, its case can't happen in practice, it
only feeds logs or metrics, the code is on its way out, or the risk is accepted. Counted
apart, so what the ignores hide can be reviewed by sort.

members.name: skipReason
members.doc: `user: unreachable: totals are rounded (ignored)`: the skip reason its mutant gets.

members.name: holdsFor
members.doc: Whether the decision still holds for the line as it is now.

types.name: Internal
types.summary: Public only so mutastic's own modules can share it: not part of the plugin API, and it may change or go in any release.
types.doc:
Public only so mutastic's own modules can share it: not part of the plugin API, and it may
change or go in any release. A plugin is written against [`Mutator`](../mutator/), [`ClassMutator`](../classmutator/) and [`Filter`](../filter/),
and the types their signatures name, less what this marks.

types.name: Listener
types.summary: Hears about a run as it happens, for progress and streamed output.
types.doc: Hears about a run as it happens, for progress and streamed output.

members.name: coverageFinished
members.doc: The coverage pass is done, and the mutants are about to run.

members.name: mutantFinished
members.doc: One mutant's result, as soon as it's known.

members.name: fileFinished
members.signature: default void fileFinished(String topLevelClass, List<MutantResult> results)
members.doc:
Every mutant in one source file's classes has its result: a top-level class and the classes
nested in it, in the order found. Comes after their `mutantFinished` calls.

members.name: mutantRevised
members.doc:
A mutant's result again, after every mutant had its first result, without a test that turned
out to fail on its own: for every mutant that test reached, caught or missed, as either result
may rest on it. It carries `falseCatchBy` when that test was the one that caught it.

types.name: Mutant
types.signature:
record Mutant(
    String className,
    String methodName,
    String descriptor,
    int ordinal,
    int line,
    Operator operator,
    String original,
    String replacement,
    Optional<String> skipped,
    List<Integer> copies,
    List<String> operands,
    Optional<String> inlinedFrom)
types.summary: One mutation of one instruction: which method, which mutation site in it (counted in bytecode order), and what the instruction becomes.
types.doc:
One mutation of one instruction: which method, which mutation site in it (counted in bytecode
order), and what the instruction becomes. A skipped mutant never runs: the change can't be told
apart from the original, or it's code no test is meant to pin.

params.name: className
params.doc: the class's internal name, `com/example/Pricing`

params.name: ordinal
params.doc: which site in the method, counted per kind of site: every arithmetic, branch and return instruction counts as an instruction site, and every call as a call site, whichever operators apply, so a new operator never shifts the ids of existing mutants

params.name: original
params.doc: the instruction: an opcode, `IF_ICMPLT`, or a call, `INVOKEVIRTUAL com/example/Audit.record(Ljava/lang/String;)V`

params.name: replacement

types.name: Mutator
types.summary: An operator a plugin adds, or a rules file describes: which instructions it changes, how, and what a missed mutant's card says.
types.doc:
An operator a plugin adds, or a rules file describes: which instructions it changes, how, and
what a missed mutant's card says. Plugins provide theirs as a `java.util.ServiceLoader` service,
in a jar `mutastic.yaml` lists under `plugins:`.

Each mutant's id is made from its method, its site and its change's label, with the operator's
id, so a change's label must never change once released. A call operator's sites are calls,
counted as the built-in call operators count them; any other operator's are every instruction in
the method, counted in order.

members.doc: The changes this operator makes at `site`, each by its label; none when it doesn't apply.

members.name: write
members.signature: void write(CodeBuilder builder, Instruction instruction, String label)
members.doc:
Writes `instruction` in its place, changed as `label` says. The stack afterwards must hold
what the original left; a change that doesn't verify is skipped as unviable, never run.

members.name: words
members.doc: What a missed mutant's card says.

types.name: Operator
types.summary: A kind of change mutastic makes: one of its own ([`BuiltIn`](../builtin/)), or one a plugin or rules file adds ([`Mutator`](../mutator/), or for a change to a class as a whole [`ClassMutator`](../classmutator/)).
types.doc:
A kind of change mutastic makes: one of its own ([`BuiltIn`](../builtin/)), or one a plugin or rules file adds
([`Mutator`](../mutator/), or for a change to a class as a whole [`ClassMutator`](../classmutator/)). How each finds its sites and
rewrites them is the engine's, or the mutator's own.

Operators work on two kinds of site, counted apart: instructions (arithmetic, branches, returns)
and calls. A new operator never shifts the ids of existing mutants.

members.doc: `mutastic/boundary`, `stream/remove-stage`: how reports, rules and `--operators` name it.

members.doc: What it changes, and when a test misses that, in plain words: for `mutastic explain`.

members.doc: Whether it works on call sites rather than instruction sites.

members.doc: Which set of operators it's in: what runs unless `--operators` says otherwise.

types.name: Operator.Tier

types.doc:
The tiers operators come in. A run takes `defaults` unless told otherwise; `stronger` adds the
operators that find more but cost more, or need more care to read; `extended` holds the
operators on modern APIs (streams, `Optional`, switch arms, regular expressions, exceptions),
chosen on top of another set: `--operators=defaults,extended`.

members.name: word
members.doc: `defaults`, `stronger`, `extended`: as `--operators` and a rules file's `tier:` take it.

The project whose mutants are this one's, run by `runner`'s tests, as `runner`'s build runs
them: its JDK, JVM arguments, working directory, tests, environment and classpath, with this
module's outputs taken off it and its own code loaded beside the mutated classes.

So is any other module of the `build` on its classpath, as one may use this module's classes:
loaded as a library, it would find none of them. A third-party library is outside the build.

types.name: ProjectSetup
types.summary: The setup file a build tool's own code writes from inside the build (Gradle's init script, Maven's extension): a properties file with what the module's tests run with.
types.doc:
The setup file a build tool's own code writes from inside the build (Gradle's init script,
Maven's extension): a properties file with what the module's tests run with. One format, so
every build tool reads it the same way.

Keys: `java`, `jvmArgs` (one per line), `workingDirectory`, and path lists joined with the
platform's separator: `classes`, `resources`, `testClasses`, `testResources`, `sources`,
`testSources`, `dependencies` (the test runtime classpath without the module's own directories).
`outputs`: what another module's classpath has of this one. Which tests run: `testIncludes` and
`testExcludes` (one class-file pattern per line, see [`TestSelection`](../testselection/)), `includeTags` and
`excludeTags` (one per line). `environment`: one `NAME=value` per line. Keys a build doesn't set
are empty.

members.doc: What's known of why the flaky test `test` is flaky, if anything is.

members.doc: The same run, with only these of its results: what's shown when the rest aren't asked about.

members.name: merge
members.doc:
This run's results with `other`'s, a run of other tests (another module's) over the same
mutants: a mutant is caught if either caught it, missed rather than not covered if either
reached it, and covered by the tests of both.

members.name: replaced
members.doc: Workers started again after one was killed for taking too long: never fewer than none.

members.name: scored
members.doc: The mutants that ran or could have: all but the skipped ones.

members.name: score
members.doc:
Detected mutants as a share of the scored ones, from 0 to 100; none when nothing was scored,
which is no evidence either way, not a perfect score.

members.doc:
Detected mutants as a share of those some test reached: how well the tests check the code they
run, apart from the code they don't. None when no test reached any; the threshold is still on
[`score`](#score).

At or above `threshold`, or nothing to score: with no mutants there is nothing to fail. Never
with a test that caught mutants and fails on its own with no mutant in: the tests aren't
sound, and a score made with them isn't trusted to pass.

The flaky tests that caught mutants, then failed on their own with no mutant in, run again
after the mutants: their catches weren't the mutants', and while there are any the run doesn't
pass.
